title: Pension fund registration: civil status, spouse and canton
goal: Collect the civil status, the spouse's date of birth (only for married employees) and the canton, so HR can register every employee with Pensionskasse Muster without missing required fields.
context: The pension fund portal requires a civil status from a fixed list: Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed (F-SC-010, F-SC-011, G-07). For Married, the portal also requires the spouse's date of birth (F-SC-012 to F-SC-014, F-SC-016, F-TR-021). It also requires a Swiss canton but does not say whether this means the residence or the work canton, and it has no option for people living abroad (F-SC-006, F-SC-007, F-SC-017). This blocks registration of cross-border employees (F-TR-035). An existing employee is in a registered partnership, which the list does not cover (F-TR-023, F-TR-024). Civil status is also an input for the source tax rule (FEAT-04).

stories.title: Provide civil status from the pension fund's list
stories.i_want: every new employee to state their civil status as one of the values on my list (Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed)
stories.so_that: HR can register the employee without the registration being rejected for a missing civil status, and the same answer can be reused for the source tax decision
stories.priority_reason: Civil status is a required field in the pension fund registration; without it the registration is blocked (F-SC-010, F-SC-015).

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status is always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee is completing onboarding
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the civil status question
acceptance_criteria.then: the question is asked to every employee and cannot be left empty, because the pension fund registration requires it

acceptance_criteria.title: Only the pension fund's civil status values can be chosen
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee answers the civil status question
acceptance_criteria.then: they choose exactly one of Single, Married, Divorced or Widowed, which is the complete list the pension fund accepts; no other value is offered

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status is received by the pension fund and source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has provided their civil status
acceptance_criteria.then: the same answer is used for the pension fund registration and as an input for the source tax decision (see FEAT-04); the employee is not asked again

acceptance_criteria.title: Statuses outside the list stay open
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee is in a registered partnership or another status not on the list (as colleague Daniel is today)
acceptance_criteria.when: they answer the civil status question
acceptance_criteria.then: no additional option is offered until it is clarified how the pension fund handles such cases (OQ-03); whether Divorced or Widowed require further details is also open (OQ-04)

stories.title: Provide the spouse's date of birth when married
stories.i_want: the date of birth of the husband or wife of every married employee, and only of married employees
stories.so_that: the registration of married employees is not blocked, while unmarried employees are not asked for spouse data we do not need
stories.priority_reason: The pension fund blocks the registration of a married employee when the spouse's date of birth is missing (F-SC-016).

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's date of birth asked only for married employees
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has stated their civil status
acceptance_criteria.then: the spouse's date of birth is asked and cannot be left empty; for any other civil status it is not asked

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's date of birth is a full date
acceptance_criteria.given: a married employee provides their spouse's date of birth
acceptance_criteria.then: it is a complete date in the form DD.MM.YYYY, as the pension fund expects (e.g. 14.06.1988)

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's date of birth is received by the pension fund
acceptance_criteria.given: a married employee has provided their spouse's date of birth
acceptance_criteria.then: the pension fund receives it as part of the registration; whether registered partners or divorced/widowed employees need partner data is open (OQ-03, OQ-04)

stories.title: Provide the canton for the pension fund
stories.i_want: Lonio to collect the Swiss canton the pension fund requires, for employees living in Switzerland
stories.so_that: I can complete the pension fund registration without returning to the employee for a missing canton
stories.priority_reason: Canton is a required pension fund field; without a value the registration is blocked, and cross-border employees currently cannot be registered at all (F-SC-006, F-SC-015, F-SC-017, F-TR-035).

acceptance_criteria.title: Canton asked only for employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has given their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: the country of the home address is Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: the canton is asked and cannot be left empty; for employees living outside Switzerland it is not asked, because the pension fund offers no option for them and what to enter is open (OQ-02)

acceptance_criteria.title: Only Swiss cantons can be chosen
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is asked for the canton
acceptance_criteria.then: they choose exactly one of the 26 cantons the pension fund lists: Aargau, Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Appenzell Innerrhoden, Basel-Landschaft, Basel-Stadt, Bern, Fribourg, Geneva, Glarus, Graubünden, Jura, Lucerne, Neuchâtel, Nidwalden, Obwalden, Schaffhausen, Schwyz, Solothurn, St. Gallen, Thurgau, Ticino, Uri, Valais, Vaud, Zug, Zurich

acceptance_criteria.title: Canton is received by the pension fund; meaning still open
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has provided the canton
acceptance_criteria.then: the pension fund receives it; whether the fund means the residence or the work canton, and what is entered for cross-border employees, must be clarified with Pensionskasse Muster (OQ-02) before this question is final
